subject: Re: FinCombo RFP — commercial clarifications (commit velocity, overage protections)
messages:

Cc: Marcus Allen <marcus.allen@fincombo.com>

Subject: FinCombo RFP — commercial clarifications

Hi Priya / Redwood team,

Thanks for the initial RFP submission. Procurement and finance had a few follow-ups specifically on the commercial section so we can move to the pricing appendix review:

1) Commit structure: Can you confirm how you define the annual commit (calendar vs. contract start)? Can customers accelerate commit payments mid-year, and if so how does that change the unit price?

2) True-up/true-down cadence: Your RFP references "monthly true-up with annual reconciliation" — does that mean we pay actual usage monthly and reconcile vs the committed annual amount at year-end? Any options for quarterly true-up?

3) Overage treatment: How are overages invoiced (per-token at overage rate, or deducted from a burst bucket)? Is there a mechanism to cap monthly overage spend?

4) Discounts and multipliers: We need visibility on multi-year/volume ladder discounts and whether seat bundles or prepaid credits change token unit economics.

5) Decommit / unwind: What is the decommit pathway and any unwind credits if we reduce commit after year 1?

Please send a short, itemized response we can circulate to legal and finance this week. If helpful, we can schedule a 30‑minute deep dive after your response.

Thanks,
Erin
Erin Cole
Director, Procurement — FinCombo Financial

Subject: FW: FinCombo RFP — commercial clarifications

Team — forwarding procurement questions from FinCombo. Drafting a concise pricing reply; want alignment on a pragmatic commercial construct that addresses their ask while protecting Redwood economics. Key constraints: predictable unit revenue, limited exposure to single-month spikes, and a clear decommit/unwind path for enterprise buyers.

High-level proposal idea (for discussion):
- Frequency-weighted commit: annual commit expressed as a 12-month token target, but invoiced monthly on a forecasted profile. True-up monthly against actuals; final year-end reconciliation with credits for overpayment. To smooth spikes we apply a 3-month moving average for true-up exposure (i.e., only months where actuals exceed the 3-month average trigger overage billing).
- Burst protection bucket: a standing monthly cushion equal to 8% of monthly forecast (not pooled across months) that absorbs transient spikes; overage rate applies only after cushion is exhausted.
- Commit velocity credits: if FinCombo increases committed run-rate >30% QoQ and sustains for 2 consecutive quarters, provide a step-down credit on the marginal rate for the incremental volume (encourages predictable growth).
- Decommit / unwind: 90-day notice for mid-year commit reduction; unwind executed as phased decommit over next 3 months with pro-rata crediting of unused pre-paid tokens at 60% of list to avoid one-off churn-driven credits. Legal to review for cause exceptions (e.g., force majeure).
- Discount ladder: base $/token at the committed band; 3 bands (0-250M, 250M-1B, 1B+). Multi-year (2-year) adds an additional 10% off committed band; prepay (annual up-front) increases discount by additional 5%.

I attached a working model (FC_pricing_model_v3.xlsx) with sample pricing cells and scenarios. Can you each take a pass and comment by EOD? Marissa — want your commercial stance. Karthik — please confirm the math and margin profile. Lauren — please flag any legal redlines on decommit wording. Aditya — note for SEA/infra routing if we need capacity reservations.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: FW: FinCombo RFP — commercial clarifications

Priya — this is a good starting point. A few comments: 

- The 3-month moving average for true-up is clever and customer-friendly; let's cap liability exposure to 225% of average monthly run-rate per month to limit extreme tail risk.
- Burst protection at 8% seems low for a finance customer with peak billing windows; propose 12% for first 6 months of the contract, then reassess.
- For commit velocity credits, let's make the step-down only apply to the incremental bucket (so we keep realized revenue on existing bands). Also require a minimum 6-month sustained run-rate before the credit triggers.
- Multi-year 10% + prepay 5% stack is fine; recommend contract language that prevents stacking with certain onboarding credits (we offer only one commercial discount program at a time).

I'll fold these into the pricing model and send a sanitized response draft to Erin. Marissa — anything else you want to call out on terms?

Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two artifacts: a short commercial response (RFP_Response_Pricing_20261105.pdf) and our working pricing model (FC_pricing_model_v3.xlsx). Summary of the commercial approach (concise bullets you can circulate to finance/legal):

1) Commit definition & invoicing:
- Annual committed tokens expressed as a 12-month target tied to contract start date.
- Invoicing: monthly invoicing based on actual usage. A monthly forecast is provided for planning; forecast changes do not change invoicing until the monthly true-up.

2) True-up cadence & smoothing:
- Monthly true-up with year-end reconciliation. To limit volatility, we apply a 3-month moving-average smoothing window when calculating month-to-month overage exposure. Practically: when actual usage spikes for a single month, the true-up references the average of that month and the prior two months to determine overage billing.
- Liability cap: maximum monthly billable overage is capped at 225% of the 3-month moving average.

3) Overage & burst protection:
- Burst protection bucket: each month Redwood reserves an allowance equal to 12% of the monthly forecast for transient spikes (first 6 months of the contract). Overages billed per-token after the cushion is exhausted at the published overage rate for the relevant band.
- Overage invoices are included on the next monthly invoice; customers can elect an optional burst-insurance add-on to cap monthly overage spend (custom pricing).

4) Discounts & multipliers:
- Tiered committed pricing bands in the model: 0–250M tokens, 250M–1B, 1B+. Unit pricing steps down at each band.
- Multi-year (2-year) committed term = additional 10% off committed band pricing.
- Prepay (annual up-front) = additional 5% off the committed band (cannot be stacked with some promotional onboarding discounts; model shows stacking rules).

5) Commit velocity & growth credits:
- Commit velocity credit: incremental step-down on marginal unit price when FinCombo increases committed run-rate >30% QoQ and sustains for 2 consecutive quarters. Credit applies only to incremental volume.

6) Decommit / unwind:
- 90-day notice required for mid-year reductions. Decommit executes as a phased 3-month reduction. Unused pre-paid tokens on unwind are credited at 60% of list unless mutually agreed otherwise. Exceptions (e.g., regulatory constraint) to be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Next steps: if this aligns with FinCombo's intent I propose a 30-minute pricing walk-through to walk the model line-by-line and confirm legal-friendly language. We can adjust the burst-protection %, velocity thresholds, and unwind credit mechanics during that call.

Available times: Fri 11/6 9:30–11:00am PST or Mon 11/9 1:00–3:00pm PST. Please let us know what works.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RFP_Response_Pricing_20261105.pdf, FC_pricing_model_v3.xlsx

- For the 3-month smoothing, can you confirm whether months 1–2 of the contract use a smaller window (obviously no prior months exist)?
- The unwind credit at 60% — will that be applied to pre-paid tokens only, or to any unused committed volume on the booking?
- On the velocity credit: can you add an example in the model showing a step-down on the marginal 300M tokens at actual numbers so finance can see the delta to the invoice?

If you can answer those 3 items in a short follow-up we’ll schedule the legal call next week. Fri AM works for a short call — Marcus and I prefer 10:00am PST.
